findings.title: --inject-dq-failure can be erased by the 'drop exact duplicates' step
findings.where: §6.2 (drops exact duplicates, then dedupe on PK) vs §6.5 / §14 (injected rows share transaction_id AND _ingested_at)
findings.problem: §6.2 runs a full-row distinct() before the PK dedupe. If the two injected rows are identical on every column (never ruled out, since only transaction_id and _ingested_at are pinned), distinct() collapses them before the uniqueness check runs and the gate does NOT fire. The 'deterministic' demo is therefore non-deterministic.
findings.fix: Pin that the two injected rows are identical on transaction_id and _ingested_at but DIFFER in at least one non-key column (e.g. amount 100.00 vs 100.01) so the full-row distinct() keeps both and only the PK-uniqueness expectation catches them. Add the sentence to §6.5 and §14.

findings.title: Bronze _rejected/ side-path and reject detection are referenced but unspecified
findings.where: §6.1 (_rejected/ with reason column, counted in lineage), §7.1 metrics.rejected_rows, §7.3 audit rejected_rows, §10 schema-cast row
findings.problem: The reject path's format, the reason-column schema, the per-row cast-failure detection rule (a Spark cast yields null, not an exception), and how input/output/rejected row counts relate are all left to the coder. Two coders would implement incompatibly and rejected_rows would mean different things.
findings.fix: Add a 'Bronze reject contract' paragraph to §6.1: detection = non-empty source value casting to null on a typed column; write rejects as Parquet with original string columns plus a _reject_reason string ('<column>:uncastable', semicolon-joined); define input_rows = output_rows + rejected_rows.

findings.title: Gold customer_360 aggregation join path risks fan-out and wrong counts
findings.where: §6.4 Mart 1 customer_360 (account_count, card_count via accounts, txn_count, last_txn_at)
findings.problem: cards joins to customers only through accounts, and the grain is one row per customer. A flat customers-accounts-cards-transactions join fans out rows so plain COUNT(txn_count) and MAX(last_txn_at) are wrong. The design mixes COUNT(DISTINCT ...) for some columns and plain COUNT for others without specifying the join strategy.
findings.fix: Specify that customer_360 is built from separate per-customer aggregations joined on customer_id (accounts metrics from accounts; card-count from accounts⋈cards; txn metrics from accounts⋈transactions), NOT one flat join before aggregating.

findings.title: landing->bronze lineage glue_table field is inconsistent with uncataloged landing
findings.where: §7.1 lineage shape (input carries glue_table) vs §2.3 (landing is not cataloged; jobs do not write tables into the landing DB)
findings.problem: The landing_to_bronze lineage input is the landing dataset, which has no Glue table, but §7.1 only shows the bronze_to_silver record. Whether glue_table is required, null, or omitted for the landing input is unspecified, so the coder guesses when serializing landing->bronze lineage.
findings.fix: State in §7.1 that glue_table is optional per input/output and omitted (or null) for uncataloged datasets (the landing input); add a landing->bronze example input without a glue_table key.

findings.title: AuditRecord optional-vs-required fields not defined for the DQ-failure path
findings.problem: On the gate-failure path the silver write never happens, so output_rows, lineage_path, emr/spark app ids have no value. The §6.2a snippet trails off with '...'. If a coder marks these required, the audit write crashes on the exact path it exists to record.
findings.fix: Mark output_rows, rejected_rows, lineage_path, emr_application_id, spark_app_id as Optional with default None, and note input_rows is populated while post-write fields are None on the DQ-failure/pre-write-fatal paths.

findings.title: Glue type mapping for register_glue_table columns is not pinned
findings.where: §5.3 register_glue_table(columns: list[tuple[str, glue_type]]) and §6.1 ((name, glue_type) from schema_defs)
findings.problem: §3 bronze types are Spark/SQL spellings; Glue StorageDescriptor.Columns needs Hive/Glue type names. The §3-type -> Glue-type mapping is not stated (e.g. int vs integer), so the coder invents it.
findings.fix: Add a one-line mapping (string->string, int->int, decimal(p,s)->decimal(p,s), date->date, timestamp->timestamp) and state schema_defs stores the Glue-compatible type string directly so no translation is needed.
